newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujitsu sees profitable 97/98 group chip business.
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu sees profitable 97/98 group chip business.

text.p: Fujitsu Ltd expects its group semiconductor business to become profitable in fiscal 1997/98, executive vice president Keizo Fukagawa said on Tuesday.
"We expect profits to grow sharply in the current 1997/98 business year but they will still not be at a satisfactory level," he told a news conference.

He said sales will grow by more than 10 percent in every sector, including chips, in 1997/98, aided by growing demand for telecommunications infrastructure, personal computers, client server systems and hard disk drives.
"We expect sales to grow in both software and hardware, as well as in services, in the computer division," Fukagawa said.
He said the firm does not expect a large decline in memory chip prices in the current business year.
Fujitsu expects an average price of 850 yen for 16MB DRAMs in the current year, down from 950 yen in the previous year, he added.
Fukagawa also said a loss in its U.S. unit Amdahl Corp dragged down its profits in 1996/97, but expects Amdahl to post profits in the current year.
Fujitsu plans capital investment of 465 billion yen in 1997/98. Of that, spending for semiconductor production equipment will be 180 billion yen, down from 192.3 billion yen in 1996/97, he said.
